thread.title: Midland ISD student-athletes sign national letters of intent
thread.title_full: Midland ISD student-athletes sign national letters of intent

author: Midland Times
title: Midland ISD student-athletes sign national letters of intent
text:
Midland Independent School District (ISD) marked a significant milestone on Wednesday as student-athletes from Midland High School and Legacy High School signed their National Letters of Intent. This event represents the next step in their academic and athletic careers.
According to the district, the group was applauded for their dedication both in the classroom and in competition. The signings were described as a reflection of years of work and commitment. Midland High’s Pulelei’ite Primus was among the prominent signees, officially committing to Vanderbilt University after receiving interest from major Division I programs nationwide. The 6-foot-4 offensive lineman had previously announced his decision on social media, selecting the Commodores over finalists Washington and Houston. Primus, recognized as one of the region’s top Class of 2026 prospects, said that Vanderbilt and Nashville felt like the right long-term fit when he made his announcement in July.
Legacy High School contributed four signees, all from its softball program. Payton Brooks and Parker Brooks signed with the University of Texas Permian Basin, while teammate Peyton Little committed to Oklahoma Panhandle State University. Fellow Rebel standout Saidy Melendez inked with Western Texas College, completing a strong group of next-level players from the Legacy roster.
Payton’s signing follows a standout year that included her selection to the Texas Girls Coaches Association (TGCA) Blue All-Star Team, an honor reserved for some of the state’s top softball talent. TGCA evaluators praised her leadership, consistency, and on-field performance—attributes that Midland ISD officials noted were evident across all of Wednesday’s signees as they prepare to take their talents to the collegiate stage.
